basic_information.official_title: AN ACT APPROPRIATING SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDS FOR THE OPERATION OF THE BANGSAMORO GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in any newspaper of general circulation in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: A ₱16.83 billion top-up to the 2026 regional budget, again funded from unspent money from earlier years. Nearly 40% of it goes to a single labour programme, and ₱2 billion sits in a Contingent Fund that includes buying the country's only Islamic bank.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Unutilised prior-year appropriations had again accumulated in the Bangsamoro Treasury. This act redistributes ₱16.83 billion of them, roughly double the size of the equivalent 2024 supplemental.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The Ministry of Labor and Employment receives ₱6.67 billion — ₱4.15 billion of it in labour and wages and ₱2.38 billion in financial assistance. Agriculture receives ₱2.75 billion, a ₱2 billion Contingent Fund covers digitalisation, Islamic finance and the acquisition of Al-Amanah Islamic Bank, and a ₱1 billion Miscellaneous Personnel Benefit Fund covers new positions and compensation adjustments.
who_will_be_affected: Workers and jobseekers, through a ₱6.67 billion employment facilitation programme
Farmers and fisherfolk, through ₱2.75 billion in agriculture support
Households, through ₱720 million for the TABANG assistance programme and ₱360 million for internet connectivity
Hajj pilgrims, through ₱76.02 million in pilgrimage financing and support
Bangsamoro Government personnel, through a ₱1 billion personnel benefit fund
Cooperatives, through ₱66.4 million in cooperative development
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2026 — approved by the Chief Minister on 21 May 2026, effective 15 days after publication. Funds run to 30 June 2028, with Personnel Services obligable only to 31 December 2027.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. ₱16.83 billion of previously unspent money, put to work through 2028. The single biggest item by far is ₱6.67 billion for employment facilitation — ₱4.15 billion of that is wages.
in_practice: ₱16,830,171,595 total across 19 agencies plus 2 special purpose funds
Funded out of unutilised prior years' appropriations from the Bangsamoro Treasury, not new revenue
Labor and Employment: ₱6.67 billion — 39.6% of the whole act, all operating expenses
Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform: ₱2.75 billion
Contingent Fund: ₱2 billion, releasable only on the Chief Minister's approval
Environment, Natural Resources and Energy: ₱1.32 billion
Office of the Chief Minister: ₱1.08 billion — ₱720 million for TABANG and ₱360 million for internet connectivity
Funds are releasable and obligable until 30 June 2028; Personnel Services only until 31 December 2027
Procurement runs through the New Government Procurement Act and PhilGEPS

for_specific_groups.Workers and jobseekers: ₱6,672,039,112 for the Employment Facilitation and Promotion Program — ₱4,152,240,800 in labour and wages, ₱2,384,650,000 in financial assistance and subsidy, and ₱14.4 million in training and scholarships. It is by a wide margin the largest allocation in the act.
for_specific_groups.Farmers, fisherfolk and agrarian reform: ₱2.75 billion, including ₱1.76 billion for Basic Integration for Harmonized Intervention, ₱823.8 million for aquaculture and capture fisheries, and ₱102.5 million for sustainable development for agrarian reform beneficiaries.
for_specific_groups.Households needing assistance: ₱720 million for Tulong Alay sa Bangsamorong Nangangailangan (TABANG), classified as supplies and materials expenses.
for_specific_groups.Communities without connectivity: ₱360 million for the Internet Connectivity Program, classified as subscription expenses.
for_specific_groups.Hajj pilgrims: ₱76,020,000 for the Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority's Hajj Financing and Support Program, entirely financial assistance and subsidy.
for_specific_groups.Cooperatives: ₱66,412,909 for the Cooperative Development Program, mostly financial assistance and subsidy.
for_specific_groups.Indigenous peoples: ₱29,220,000 for Indigenous Peoples' Development Initiatives — 0.2% of the act, though 8.6 times the ₱3.4 million allocated in the 2024 supplemental.
for_specific_groups.Patients: ₱490,374,060 for health, including ₱377.0 million for the Tiyakap Bangsamoro Kalusugan programme and ₱61.6 million for non-communicable disease.
for_specific_groups.Government personnel: ₱1 billion in the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefit Fund for salaries, bonuses, allowances, newly created positions and compensation adjustments — released only where the finance ministry determines the requirement cannot be met from an agency's own Personnel Services appropriation under BAA 85.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM, with funds released directly to ministries, offices and agencies including their provincial offices.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Release and obligation run to 30 June 2028; construction completion, delivery and payment to 31 December 2028.
what_you_can_do: Ask the labour ministry how the Employment Facilitation and Promotion Program is administered in your area — it is the largest single allocation in this act
Check ministry websites for infrastructure disclosures required within 30 days of contract and of completion
Look for quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports, due within 30 days of each quarter's end for the Contingent Fund and Personnel Benefit Fund
Procurement is conducted through PhilGEPS, which is searchable
watch_out_for: ₱6.67 billion — 39.6% of the act — sits in one programme line at one ministry, of which ₱4.15 billion is labour and wages. In the 2024 supplemental the same ministry received ₱148 million.
This act was passed on 20 May 2026 and approved the next day, in the closing period of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament before the first elected Parliament.
The ₱2 billion Contingent Fund is released only on the Chief Minister's approval, and its stated uses include 'other expenditures' covering unforeseen initiatives not otherwise in the act.
The act again spends money earlier budgets did not use — ₱16.83 billion this time, roughly double the 2024 figure.
Personnel Services appropriations expire earlier than the rest, on 31 December 2027, with an extended payment window to 31 March 2028.

key_terms_explained.Supplemental appropriation: A budget law passed during the year adding to what the annual appropriations act provided.
key_terms_explained.Unutilised prior years' appropriations: Money appropriated in earlier budgets but never obligated or released. This act's entire funding source.
key_terms_explained.Contingent Fund: A reserve for new or urgent projects arising during the year, released case by case on the Chief Minister's approval.
key_terms_explained.MPBF: Miscellaneous Personnel Benefit Fund — a central pot for salary, bonus and allowance requirements agencies cannot meet from their own personnel budgets.
key_terms_explained.TABANG: Tulong Alay sa Bangsamorong Nangangailangan — an assistance programme run from the Office of the Chief Minister.
key_terms_explained.Al-Amanah Islamic Bank: Al-Amanah Islamic Investment Bank of the Philippines, the country's only Islamic bank. The Contingent Fund may be used for the cost of acquiring it.
key_terms_explained.PhilGEPS: The Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System, designated here as the primary platform for all Bangsamoro Government procurement.
key_terms_explained.Cash budgeting system: Appropriations valid for obligation only within a fixed window, after which they lapse and unobligated balances revert.

for_citizens: None. An appropriations act imposes no duty on the public.
for_agencies: Secure a Special Allotment Release Order before obligating appropriations
Obtain a Certification of Availability of Funds from the chief accountant before incurring any obligation, made an integral part of every contract
Procure through PhilGEPS under RA 12009 and its 2025 implementing rules
Obtain the Chief Minister's Authority to Purchase Motor Vehicle before buying transportation equipment
Submit quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports within 30 days of each quarter's end for the Contingent Fund and Personnel Benefit Fund
Submit a status report on Commission on Audit findings within 60 days of the annual audit report, and post it on the agency website
Post infrastructure project details, winning contractor, actual cost and variation orders on the agency website within 30 days

what_is_prohibited: Incurring an obligation without first securing a Certification of Availability of Funds from the agency's chief accountant.
Procuring transportation equipment without the Chief Minister's Authority to Purchase Motor Vehicle.

Treating funds transferred between organisational units, between agencies, or to LGUs as disbursed before the goods, works or services have actually been delivered, inspected and accepted within the validity period.
Deducting engineering and administrative overhead above 1%, or administrative costs above 3%, of project costs for projects over ₱1,000,000.
Obligating appropriations after the validity period.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence.
penalties.for_officials: Failure to submit the required financial and physical accountability reports results in the automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until compliance. Repeated failure or refusal without justifiable cause may constitute grounds for administrative disciplinary action under civil service rules.

where_to_complain.audit: The Commission on Audit, whose annual audit report each agency must answer within 60 days

everyday_scenarios: A jobseeker is hired into a short-term government-funded work programme. The ₱4.15 billion 'labour and wages' line under employment facilitation is the largest source of such funding in this act.
A household receives assistance under TABANG. ₱720 million was appropriated for it here, through the Office of the Chief Minister.
A pilgrim receives Hajj financing support. ₱76.02 million was appropriated to the Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority, entirely as financial assistance and subsidy.

A resident wants to check who won a contract. Section 13 requires the agency to post the project title, location, description, approved budget estimates and winning contractor within 30 days of contract execution.
A ministry stops filing accountability reports. Section 12 automatically suspends the salaries of the responsible officials until they comply.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Appropriation of Funds, made “out of the unutilized prior years' appropriations from the Bangsamoro Treasury”. Agency totals for the FY 2026 supplemental appropriation: Labor and Employment ₱6,672,039,112; Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform ₱2,750,790,000; Environment, Natural Resources and Energy ₱1,321,000,000; the Office of the Chief Minister ₱1,080,000,000; Health ₱490,374,060; Public Works ₱489,102,000; Human Settlements and Development ₱228,000,000; Public Order and Safety ₱151,450,000; Basic, Higher and Technical Education ₱145,284,000; Science and Technology ₱126,192,872; Social Services and Development ₱102,191,174; the Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority ₱76,020,000; the Cooperatives and Social Enterprise Authority ₱66,412,909; Transportation and Communications ₱61,156,780; Indigenous Peoples' Affairs ₱29,220,000; the Bangsamoro Sports Commission ₱21,000,000; the Bangsamoro Youth Commission ₱12,880,000; the Bangsamoro Science High School ₱4,858,688; and Trade, Investment and Tourism ₱2,200,000. Two special purpose funds follow: the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefit Fund ₱1,000,000,000 and the Contingent Fund ₱2,000,000,000 — a total of ₱16,830,171,595.

Section 1 (programme detail) — The Employment Facilitation and Promotion Program at the labour ministry takes ₱6,672,039,112 in a single line, comprising ₱4,152,240,800 in labour and wages, ₱2,384,650,000 in financial assistance and subsidy, ₱115,710,226.50 in other operating expenses and ₱14,418,085.50 in training and scholarships. The Office of the Chief Minister's ₱1.08 billion covers Tulong Alay sa Bangsamorong Nangangailangan (TABANG) at ₱720,000,000 and the Internet Connectivity Program at ₱360,000,000. Agriculture's largest lines are Basic Integration for Harmonized Intervention ₱1,758,047,000 and Integrated and Sustainable Development for Aquaculture/Capture ₱823,790,000. The environment ministry's ₱1.32 billion is dominated by Natural Resources Policy Enforcement, Conservation and Development at ₱1,240,000,000. Health's largest line is Tiyakap Bangsamoro Kalusugan at ₱377,036,800. Public works is entirely capital outlay. The Pilgrimage Authority's ₱76,020,000 is a Hajj Financing and Support Program, wholly financial assistance and subsidy.

Special Provisions, Miscellaneous Personnel Benefit Fund — The ₱1,000,000,000 is for personnel benefits used for deficiencies in authorised salaries, bonuses, allowances, associated premiums and other similar benefits, covering the funding requirement of newly created positions for offices that may be created, compensation adjustments as authorised by law, and other incentives authorised by law or by issuances of the Chief Minister. Release is subject to the finance ministry's determination that the Personnel Services requirement cannot be accommodated within the agency's own appropriations under Section 44 of the General Provisions of BAA 85, the FY 2026 General Appropriations Act. Implementing agencies submit quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports within 30 days of each quarter's end.

Special Provisions, Contingent Fund — The ₱2,000,000,000 covers new or urgent projects and activities of ministries, offices and agencies needing implementation or payment during the year, including: the digitalization of the BARMM bureaucracy; a Transitional Development Impact Fund, with the implementing agency primarily responsible for implementation and monitoring; Islamic Finance Programs, subject to Section 30 of BAA 85; “provision for cost of acquisition of Al-Amanah Islamic Bank and other related costs”; customs duties and taxes including tax expenditures and assumed tax payable on foreign assistance and donations to the Bangsamoro, such as Japan Government Assistance; infrastructure necessary for establishing the Bangsamoro Government Center; and other expenditures supporting programmes mandated by law, including unforeseen initiatives not covered by the act, subject to technical assessment and the Chief Minister's approval. Release requires the Chief Minister's approval on the finance ministry's recommendation after technical assessment and review of documentary requirements including indicative programme plans, construction plans and programme of works, indicative procurement plan, cost-benefit analysis and list of beneficiaries. Quarterly reports must be submitted and published on the agency website.

Sections 2–4 (General Provisions) — A Special Allotment Release Order authorises agencies to obligate appropriations. Government funds must be used in accordance with the appropriations authorised. Agencies must strictly adhere to RA 12009, the New Government Procurement Act, and its 2025 implementing rules, along with Government Procurement Policy Board issuances; and “the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) shall be the primary source of information and platform for the conduct of all procurement activities of the Bangsamoro Government”.

Sections 5–8 — Engineering and administrative overhead not exceeding 1% of project funds, and administrative costs not exceeding 3% of project costs, may be deducted for projects costing more than ₱1,000,000. All transportation equipment outlays require the Chief Minister's Authority to Purchase Motor Vehicle on the finance ministry's recommendation. No obligation may be incurred without first securing a Certification of Availability of Funds from the agency's chief accountant, made an integral part of the signed contract.

Section 9 — Cash Budgeting System. Appropriations are available for release and obligation until 30 June 2028, but Personnel Services appropriations are valid for obligation and disbursement only until 31 December 2027, with an extended payment period to 31 March 2028 in exceptional circumstances. Disbursement of maintenance and operating expenses and capital outlays is generally due by 30 June 2028, with completion of construction, inspection and payment of infrastructure capital outlays, and delivery, inspection and payment of other items, by 31 December 2028. After the validity period all unreleased appropriations, unobligated allotments and obligated allotments for goods, services or projects not yet delivered, rendered or completed revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation under Section 19, Article XII of RA 11054. Transfers between organisational units, between agencies, or to local government units are not considered disbursed until actually used to pay for completed construction, goods delivered and services rendered, inspected and accepted within the validity period.

Sections 10–15 — Funds are released directly to ministries, offices and agencies including their provincial offices and organisational units. Agencies must submit a status report on Commission on Audit findings within 60 days of the annual audit report, furnishing copies to the finance ministry, the Speaker and Parliament's Committee on Finance, Budget and Management, and posting it on the agency website. Financial and physical accountability reports must be submitted monthly, quarterly or annually in hardcopy, electronically and on the agency website, with failure resulting in “the automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until compliance is made”, and repeated failure constituting grounds for administrative disciplinary action. Transparency in Infrastructure Projects requires posting the project title, location and detailed description, the estimates behind the Approved Budget for the Contract, and the winning contractor with the awarded bid estimates within 30 calendar days of executing the contract, and the detailed actual cost with any variation orders within 30 calendar days of the certificate of completion. A separability clause follows, and the act takes effect 15 days after publication.

related_legislation.related_note: Supplements BAA 85, the FY 2026 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, which it cross-references for Personnel Services rules (Section 44 of its General Provisions) and Islamic finance programmes (its Section 30). Reversion of unobligated funds follows Section 19, Article XII of RA 11054, and procurement follows RA 12009, the New Government Procurement Act, with its 2025 implementing rules. The cash budgeting system and the automatic salary suspension for non-reporting mirror Sections 35 and 75 of BAA 84, the Bangsamoro Budget System Act of 2025. Islamic finance funding connects to Section 32, Article XII of the Organic Law.

implementation_status.irr_status: None required. The finance ministry may issue guidelines on the cash budgeting system, on Contingent Fund releases, and on the reporting and release of funds.

implementing_agency.agency: The 19 ministries, offices and agencies receiving appropriations, with the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management issuing release orders and the Chief Minister approving Contingent Fund releases

citizen_questions.q: How much is this, and where did the money come from?
citizen_questions.a: ₱16,830,171,595, appropriated out of unutilised prior years' appropriations held in the Bangsamoro Treasury — money earlier budgets did not spend. It is not new revenue.

The Ministry of Labor and Employment's Employment Facilitation and Promotion Program, at ₱6,672,039,112 — 39.6% of the entire act. Of that, ₱4,152,240,800 is labour and wages and ₱2,384,650,000 is financial assistance and subsidy.

citizen_questions.q: What is the Contingent Fund for?
citizen_questions.a: ₱2 billion for new or urgent projects during the year — digitalising the BARMM bureaucracy, a Transitional Development Impact Fund, Islamic finance programmes, the cost of acquiring Al-Amanah Islamic Bank, customs duties and taxes on foreign assistance including Japanese government aid, infrastructure for the Bangsamoro Government Center, and other unforeseen initiatives. Release requires the Chief Minister's approval on the finance ministry's recommendation.

citizen_questions.q: Is the region buying a bank?
citizen_questions.a: The Contingent Fund's special provisions expressly include “provision for cost of acquisition of Al-Amanah Islamic Bank and other related costs”. Al-Amanah is the country's only Islamic bank, and the acquisition connects to the Organic Law's mandate to develop an Islamic banking and finance system in the region.

citizen_questions.q: How long is the money available?
citizen_questions.a: Appropriations are releasable and obligable until 30 June 2028. Personnel Services are valid only until 31 December 2027, with payment extendable to 31 March 2028 in exceptional cases. Infrastructure completion and payment run to 31 December 2028.
Yes. ₱76,020,000 for the Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority's Hajj Financing and Support Program, entirely as financial assistance and subsidy.

citizen_questions.q: How does this compare with the 2024 supplemental?
citizen_questions.a: It is roughly double. BAA 63 appropriated ₱8.44 billion for FY 2024; this appropriates ₱16.83 billion for FY 2026. The composition also shifted sharply: agriculture led the 2024 act at 43.6%, while labour leads this one at 39.6% — the labour ministry's allocation rose from ₱148 million to ₱6.67 billion.

Through PhilGEPS, which this act designates as the primary source of information and platform for all Bangsamoro Government procurement, under the New Government Procurement Act and its 2025 implementing rules.

views.simple: A ₱16.83 billion supplemental budget for 2026, funded entirely from prior years' unspent appropriations. The Ministry of Labor and Employment takes ₱6.67 billion — 39.6% of the act, with ₱4.15 billion of it in wages — followed by agriculture at ₱2.75 billion, a ₱2 billion Contingent Fund covering digitalisation, Islamic finance and the acquisition of Al-Amanah Islamic Bank, environment at ₱1.32 billion, and ₱1.08 billion at the Office of the Chief Minister for the TABANG assistance programme and internet connectivity. Funds run to 30 June 2028, procurement goes through PhilGEPS, and officials who fail to report lose their salaries until they comply.
